items.title: India’s economic resilience strengthens global leadership prospects: Jean-Pierre Landau
items.summary: Amidst ongoing geopolitical tensions and global economic uncertainty, India is showcasing remarkable resilience, paving the way for enhanced leadership. This trajectory is supported by a steady growth in exports and robust foreign investment. However, the emergence of artificial intelligence necessitates urgent workforce training initiatives. Addressing both technical and non-technical skills in training programs will be vital for equipping future job seekers as the economy adapts to technological advancements.

items.title: Single-window GST registration for multistate businesses set for pilot this week
items.summary: In a significant move, the central government is set to implement a consolidated goods and services tax registration system for businesses operating across multiple states. This innovative system will facilitate a single application process, minimizing the administrative challenges associated with multiple submissions. It is worth mentioning that small taxpayers under the composition scheme will not be eligible for this benefit.

items.title: Silicon Valley companies discuss simpler GST, customs rules with CBIC
items.summary: CBIC chairman Vivek Chaturvedi met a delegation led by Shefali Goradia, chairperson, Deloitte, South Asia and the Silicon Valley Tax Directors Group (SVTDG), which brings together tax directors and finance executives from more than 100 leading US technology companies, primarily headquartered in the Silicon Valley region.

items.title: Siberia's 'mysterious illness': All about bubonic plague, how it spreads and whether the world should worry
items.summary: In response to a laboratory worker's suspected death from bubonic plague, Russian officials have enforced quarantine protocols. Approximately 200 individuals are under watch for potential exposure to the infection, which mainly spreads via flea bites or contact with infected wildlife. Despite its serious nature, bubonic plague is treatable with antibiotics, though the pneumonic variant poses a greater threat due to its direct human transmission.

items.title: Two-wheelers dominate work commutes, buses lead overnight travel: NHTS survey
items.summary: The latest National Household Travel Survey reveals that two-wheelers dominate daily commuting choices, while buses make up over 50% of overnight travel, underscoring their role in long-distance journeys. Urban workers face higher commuting costs than their rural counterparts, and students mostly use walking and buses to get to school. The survey illustrates varied travel habits across states, emphasizing the significance of public transport options.

items.title: Treasuries Slump Pushes Long-End Yields to Fresh 24-Year Highs
items.summary: Treasuries came under renewed pressure Monday, pushing longer-dated yields to fresh multi-decade peaks as bonds extended their monthslong slide.

items.title: DG can perform depositary functions: WTO tells India
items.summary: In response to India's questions on the legal basis by which the WTO director general is assigned the role of acting as the depositary of the Interim Arrangements for the Agreement on Electronic Commerce (ECA), the organisation said that serving as a depositary of the ECA would not conflict with the chief's role and responsibilities.

items.title: Hospital pricing part of wider value chain: Max MD
items.summary: Abhay Soi, chairman of Max Healthcare, commented on scrutiny regarding hospital pricing in India. He stated that hospitals should be evaluated based on the entire clinical process rather than individual consumable prices. Soi explained that the administration of medical supplies involves significant training and compliance with storage and disposal regulations. He noted that hospitals have multiple billing items with varying margins contributing to an overall profit margin.

items.title: Centre may seek legal view on licensing of sterile drugs
items.summary: The government is actively exploring a proposal to expand central licensing authority over all sterile drug products following a recent Supreme Court decision that restricted the enforcement authority of central officials. A meeting of the drugs consultative committee underscored the essential requirement for specialized regulatory oversight for these sensitive products, aiming for uniform regulations. A dedicated sub-committee will evaluate the proposal's feasibility and gather legal insights before any definitive actions.

items.title: Mid-sized restaurants hungry for funds as investors stay away
items.summary: Mid-sized organized restaurant chains such as Punjab Grill and Mad Over Donuts face financing challenges. Investors are being more cautious, focusing on sustainable profits and unit economics. As a result, several chains explore capital raises or stake sales. Recent investments favor businesses demonstrating strong financial performance and growth potential. Meanwhile, larger investments continue to thrive, creating a divide in the restaurant industry.

items.title: Oil ministry plans centralised R&D mechanism to steer projects, funding in oil and gas sector
items.summary: The oil ministry aims to establish a centralised mechanism for research and development in the oil and gas sector. This approach will align initiatives from state-run companies and other organizations with national priorities. The proposed Centre for High Technology will coordinate R&D project allocation, funding, and monitoring. State firms will maintain ownership of their R&D while working collaboratively with other entities.

items.title: 'Great achievements already made': Swiss President Parmelin on India-EFTA trade pact's first year
items.summary: The India-European Free Trade Association Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement has been effective since its implementation a year ago. Swiss President Guy Parmelin stated that strong interest from companies has been evident in various sectors. This agreement is expected to significantly enhance bilateral trade and attract long-term investment. Additionally, Switzerland seeks to strengthen cooperation in business and technology during the President's current visit.

items.title: Starbucks recovery plan is working. Here's how Mike Khouw says to trade the coffee giant
items.summary: Mike Khouw breaks down how he's trading Starbucks through options.

items.title: Sumitomo buys 49% in Hero Future Energies unit for Rs 375 crore
items.summary: Japan's Sumitomo Corporation has made a strategic investment by acquiring a 49% interest in a Hero Future Energies subsidiary for ₹375 crore, leaving Hero with a controlling 51% stake. This renewable energy project, based in Bidar, Karnataka, aims to produce 500 MW of electricity. Hero Future Energies' impressive 10 GW renewable energy portfolio underlines the significance of this partnership in Sumitomo's ambitions in India's growing energy sector.

items.title: Amazon wants Prime members to get more than just early access this festive season
items.summary: Amazon is introducing extra benefits for Prime members during the festive season, starting with the Great Indian Festival. Prime members will enjoy additional discounts and cashback offers on various products. The company emphasises faster delivery, with same-day deliveries becoming increasingly common. With growth in membership from smaller cities, this initiative aims to create consistent value for customers.

items.title: National Housing Bank likely to double affordable housing outlay for HFCs this fiscal
items.summary: National Housing Bank plans to double the refinance and affordable housing funds for large housing finance companies. These funds will be available to companies seeking long-term and cheaper financing options. LIC Housing Finance, Bajaj Housing Finance, and others are likely to benefit from this increase. The funding is expected to help reduce reliance on banks while promoting growth in housing loans.

items.title: French bond contagion fears are rattling the euro
items.summary: The value of the euro has declined significantly as French borrowing costs increase. Concerns are rising among European policymakers regarding potential contagion across the euro area. The French government's proposed budget aims to reduce its high debt while facing strong political opposition. Investors are shifting from French bonds to safer German debts amid these tensions. Analysts predict that the euro may test lower thresholds if fiscal issues persist in Europe.

items.title: FPIs turn cautious on Indian stocks amid global headwinds; what could improve the foreign flow outlook
items.summary: Foreign portfolio investors shifted to net selling in September, offloading stocks worth ₹35,860 crore, continuing into October with ₹18,513 crore. This trend caused the Nifty to decline 14% year-to-date, its worst since 2011, as geopolitical tensions and surging bond yields deter investments.

items.title: PTC shares soar nearly 34% after Schneider Electric agrees to $22.6 billion buyout
items.summary: In a strategic move, Schneider Electric has agreed to acquire PTC for $22.6 billion in cash. The acquisition reflects ongoing shifts in the software industry due to artificial intelligence disruption. PTC's board approved the offer, which represents a significant premium compared to its recent share price. Schneider plans to finance the transaction through a combination of debt and new shares issuance.

This decision has led to a dispute with representatives from Aeroflot and Volga Dnepr regarding previously arranged shipments. Currently, approximately 2.5 tonnes of cargo is lying in the airport warehouse while additional cargo seeks transportation. Delmos Aviation has requested intervention from the Ministry of Civil Aviation to resolve the matter.

items.title: Finmin to meet heads of banks on Tuesday to review progress of financial inclusion scheme
items.summary: A meeting involving bank heads is scheduled for Tuesday to assess the progress of financial inclusion schemes. Key initiatives include Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana and Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana, which support small enterprises. Other schemes such as PM Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana and PM Suraksha Bima Yojana offer insurance coverage for different age groups. The StandUp India Scheme focuses on empowering SC, ST, and women borrowers.

items.title: Mercedes-Maybach S 580e launches in India with only 30 units on offer: Check price, full features list
items.summary: Mercedes-Benz India has launched the Maybach S 580e plug-in hybrid priced at Rs 3.35 crore. This model is the first plug-in hybrid in the Maybach range offered in India. It features a combination of a six-cylinder petrol engine and an electric motor for enhanced performance. The luxury car provides a range of up to 98 km on a full charge with various safety features included.

items.title: EXPLAINER: Why are airlines and Adani Airports at odds?
items.summary: Mumbai's Terminal 1 is set for redevelopment starting in January 2027, which has led to a flight reduction dispute. Airlines are concerned about shifting international flights to the new Navi Mumbai International Airport as it affects their operations. MIAL has planned to temporarily reduce international departures from Terminal 2 while accommodating displaced domestic passengers. The Civil Aviation Ministry is meeting with stakeholders to resolve the issue and finalize flight allocations.

items.summary: Beijing shuttered 670 mainly rural banks last year in a bid to create fewer, larger and better-capitalized lenders.

items.title: SAIL H1 hot metal output 10.2 MT, up 2% on year
items.summary: Steel Authority of India Ltd has set a new benchmark with a record hot metal production of 10.2 million tonnes for the period of April to September 2026. The company also achieved significant figures in crude and finished steel production, totaling 9.6 million and 8.39 million tonnes respectively. Notably, high-end steel saw a remarkable production of around 2 million tonnes, while September marked the highest saleable steel sales at 1.

Marico reported a double-digit volume growth, while Godrej tracked revenue growth in the teens despite inflationary risks. items.title: German Mittelstand expands engineering and technology operations in India
items.summary: German mid-sized companies are increasingly expanding their engineering and technology operations in India, particularly in Bengaluru. More than 80 German companies operate over 150 global capability centre (GCC) units employing over 130,000 professionals. Access to engineering talent and skilled professionals in India drives this rapid growth, which has seen GCCs grow by 108% in five years. Many of these companies now collaborate with universities and startups to enhance capabilities further.

items.title: Haldia to revamp feedstock mix after Mideast war hit supplies, executive says
items.summary: In response to disruptions from the Middle East conflict, Haldia Petrochemicals Ltd is set to broaden its feedstock sourcing strategies. Currently reliant on 50% local supply and 50% from the Middle East, HPL plans to enhance its processing abilities by using condensate and up to 30% LPG at its West Bengal facility next year.

items.summary: Tata Steel is channeling Rs 40,000 crore towards boosting the capacity of Neelachal Ispat Nigam Limited (NINL) by an impressive 5 million tonnes annually. This strategic acquisition, which was finalized on July 4, 2022, cost Rs 12,100 crore. After being idle for over three years due to financial turmoil, NINL is now revived.

items.title: India luxury car sales rise in double digits; Mercedes-Benz sales grow 8% to record 15,190 units
items.summary: The luxury vehicle market in India showcased a striking uptick in sales for 2026, reflecting a robust appetite for high-end automobiles. Mercedes-Benz led the way with impressive sales reaching 15,190 units in just the first nine months, bolstered by exciting new launches and upgrades from loyal customers despite supply challenges. Electric models, particularly with the CLA Electric's introduction, further supported this growth.

items.title: Navi Mumbai International Airport rolls out multimodal connectivity ahead of winter schedule
items.summary: Navi Mumbai International Airport is set to enhance its transport network with affordable options for passengers. Multiple services include buses, taxis, and airport shuttles, offering economical travel across regions. The Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation will begin the e-Shivai bus operations on October 7 for passengers. Besides, ride-sharing services such as Bharat Taxi and Uber will be available starting October 10.
